paper.title_en: Improvements on quantum designated-verifier signature based on Bell states
paper.abstract_en: Quantum designated-verifier signature (QDVS) is a cryptographic scheme based on quantum mechanics in which a signature can be verified only by a specific designated verifier. Recently, Xin et al. [31 ] proposed a QDVS scheme based on Bell states and claimed that it was secure. However, we demonstrate that their scheme is vulnerable to forgery attacks. To overcome this vulnerability, we propose an improved QDVS scheme utilizing single qubits, a secret random permutation, and unitary operations. Security analysis shows that the proposed scheme satisfies the required designated-verifier security properties while resisting various attacks. Compared with representative QDVS schemes, our scheme requires neither a third party (TP) nor quantum entanglement resources, and achieves a qubit efficiency of $100\%$ with a quantum cost of one qubit per signed bit and only two quantum communication rounds.
